summary_text:
On January 8, 2024, the patient sustained a left arm industrial machinery entrapment injury, resulting in a crush injury to the left arm with complete mechanical disruption, bone protrusion, and a cold, pulseless hand. A factory responder applied a tourniquet to the left arm, and emergency crews dismantled the machine to free the arm. The patient received IV fentanyl 100mcg and was noted to have a GCS of 11 with a reported brief loss of consciousness. He was transferred to Midwest Regional trauma unit, where Dr. David Cho, MD, FACEP, diagnosed a complete traumatic amputation at a level between the shoulder and elbow, with complete brachial artery and nerve transection, exposed bone, and massive soft tissue loss, producing traumatic shock from blood loss. X-ray and CT angiography of the left humerus, elbow, and forearm demonstrated a comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, open segmental forearm/hand fractures, and carpal disorganization; angiography confirmed brachial artery disruption. The limb was deemed unsalvageable. The patient received 2 units of packed red blood cells and was taken emergently to surgery.

Dr. Marcus Vance, MD, FACS, performed a left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation with myofascial closure, bone beveling, ligation and division of the brachial artery, and traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves with 0.5% bupivacaine injection; the humerus was sectioned at the junction of the middle and distal thirds. A JP drain was placed, and the patient was admitted to the ICU postoperatively, receiving additional PRBCs and lactated Ringers. Postoperative care included Dilaudid PCA transitioned to oral oxycodone and gabapentin 300mg TID, IV Ancef, and wound care; the JP drain was removed January 12, 2024, and he was discharged on cefdinir 300mg BID and gabapentin.

By February 12, 2024, he reported phantom limb pain rated 8/10 and stump hypersensitivity; gabapentin was increased to 600mg TID and desensitization therapy was initiated. By June 18, 2024, a tender 1.5 cm nodule at the medial residual border was identified as a post-amputation neuroma of the ulnar/median nerves, prompting surgery. On November 12, 2024, Dr. Vance excised a 1.8 x 1.4 cm neuroma and transposed the median and ulnar nerve stumps into the triceps muscle with 5-0 epineural sutures.

Prosthetic fitting began February 5, 2025, with a custom myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis and electrode calibration, followed by structured PT with Sarah Jenkins, PT, DPT, through 2026. Treatment lapsed with no-shows on May 12, 2025 and November 10, 2025, attributed by the patient to holiday workload and transportation issues. He completed his rehabilitation program on June 22, 2026, achieving near-normal left shoulder range of motion and returning to modified light/medium duty work. Notably, a 2022 left shoulder AC joint sprain and rotator cuff tendinitis, treated conservatively, predated this injury.
